You are shown a snapshot of US macroeconomic and market data as it was known at the end of one month between 2007 and 2026.

Estimate which month the snapshot describes. Use only the figures supplied plus your general knowledge of economic history.

Reply with one JSON object and nothing else:
{"year": yyyy, "month": m, "confidence": c, "cues": ["...", "..."]}
Rules: year is an integer from 2007 to 2026; month is an integer from 1 to 12; c in [0, 1] is your confidence that the guess is within 6 months of the truth; 1 to 3 short cues citing the inputs.
text:
This looks like late 2016. Unemployment is 5.0%, the fed funds rate is 0.37%, and the 10-year yield is 1.85%. Headline CPI is 1.14% year over year, and core CPI is 2.15%.

The 10-year at 1.85% with a 12-month change of -0.27 fits either November or December 2016, though the 10-year was around 2.4% by December. The fed funds rate at 0.37% fits October 2016, when the effective rate was about 0.40%. In September it was 0.29%, and in October 0.40%, so this is probably October.

US equity returned 1.3% over 12 months, and the 3-month return was 6.5%. Emerging-market equity was down 17.3% over 12 months, which matches the year to October 2016 less well but is plausible. Gold fell 6.1% in the month, which fits October 2016 (gold dropped from about 1315 to 1270). The VIX at 13 doesn't fit October 2016, though, since it was around 13 at month-end in October and rose to about 14 in November. Industrial production at -1.07% year over year also fits late 2016.

The 10-year at 1.85% matches the end of October 2016. The dollar's 12-month change of -8.64 looks odd, but it is probably a quirk of how that series is measured.

The unemployment rate rose 0.1 over 3 months, which could be 4.9 to 5.0 in 2016. That fits October 2016, when the published figure was 4.9, so the snapshot may describe a different month. Still, the evidence points to a month near October 2016.

Equity 12-month returns were around 4% by October 2016, so +1.3% is slightly low. Gold's 6-month return of +14.6% is consistent with the period.

Alternatively, this could be a month in early 2016. The unemployment rate was 5.0% in January and February 2016, and the 10-year was 1.85% in February 2016 at around 1.74%. Core CPI at 2.15% fits that time too. But the fed funds rate in early 2016 was about 0.34-0.38, and US equity's 12-month return of +1.3% fits end of January 2016 or end of October 2016 about equally. Gold's -6.1% 1-month drop fits October better than January 2016, when gold rose. The VIX falling 7.43 over 3 months, and the 3-month equity return of +6.5%, fit October 2016 rather than early 2016, when equities fell. I'll go with October 2016.
